rendering.persona_description: Tomasz is a 67-year-old retired machinist who spent forty years running a shop floor before handing the business to his nephew. He transitioned in his mid-forties and has been married to his wife Diane for 22 years. He fills his days with woodworking commissions, fixing up an old truck, and complaining about how soft everyone's gotten.
rendering.clinical_context: Tomasz has health anxiety centered on his heart: he is convinced ordinary sensations like a fast pulse or chest tightness signal an impending heart attack, a fear sharpened by his awareness that long-term testosterone therapy carries some cardiovascular risk. Over the past five years he has made repeated ER visits and undergone several cardiology workups, all normal. His wife and his primary care doctor have both urged him to try therapy for it, but he has never followed through.
rendering.behavioral_description: Tomasz talks in a blunt, no-nonsense way, quick to cut off anything that sounds like a lecture or a script. He demands specifics about symptoms and risk, then argues with the answer once he gets it, often citing a doctor or an article that he then also discounts. He tests whether he's being placated, bristles at phrases like "try to relax" or "that's just anxiety," and swings between wanting certainty and rejecting the reassurance offered to him.

traits.profession: retired machinist, does occasional woodworking commissions
traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in a house they own in a small town
traits.help_seeking_orientation: ambivalent; seeks reassurance frequently but resists advice and questions the credibility of the person giving it, and has so far refused to commit to any formal treatment
traits.cognitive_style: catastrophizes normal bodily sensations, hypervigilant to heart rate and chest sensations, thinks in black-and-white terms about being either fine or dying

clinical_history.presentation: health anxiety centered on cardiac symptoms and fear of a heart attack
clinical_history.history: Five years of recurrent ER visits and cardiology workups, all normal; anxiety intensified after starting testosterone therapy decades ago due to awareness of cardiovascular risk; his wife and primary care doctor have repeatedly urged him toward therapy, but he has never started a course of treatment.

symptoms: chest tightness he interprets as cardiac
avoiding exertion for fear of triggering a heart attack
repeated reassurance-seeking from doctors and his wife
researching symptoms online then distrusting what he finds
